description: Whether every workload is sized right: what it asks for against what it used over the range, per workload, namespace and pool.

panels.description: Requests against use, over the range. CPU idle: requested minus used at p95, per container, times its pods; memory idle likewise with the range's maximum. Workloads: one dot each, by state. OOM kills: restarts of a container whose last termination was OOMKilled. Based on: how much of the range Prometheus holds. States: idle uses under 30 % of its request, fits 30 to 100 %, short more than its request, near limit a container's memory maximum over 80 % of its limit (it wins over the others), unset asks for nothing. A workload is a Deployment, StatefulSet or DaemonSet (kube_pod_owner, and kube_replicaset_owner for a Deployment); per pod, its containers are summed, each at its largest across the pods. Jobs, CronJobs and static pods are left out.

panels.title: Pools
panels.description: Per pool (0xc0.cc/pool): the track is what its nodes can allocate, the light bar what running and pending pods ask for (Jobs and static pods included), the solid bar what every container used together, at the 95th percentile over the range.

panels.title: Asked vs used · CPU
panels.description: Each bubble is a workload, sized by its pods: its CPU request per pod against its use at the 95th percentile of rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total[5m]) over the range. The dashed line is a perfect fit. Hover a bubble for its numbers and the suggested request (p95 × 1.2, in steps of 10m). States: idle uses under 30 % of its request, fits 30 to 100 %, short more than its request, near limit a container's memory maximum over 80 % of its limit (it wins over the others), unset asks for nothing. A workload is a Deployment, StatefulSet or DaemonSet (kube_pod_owner, and kube_replicaset_owner for a Deployment); per pod, its containers are summed, each at its largest across the pods. Jobs, CronJobs and static pods are left out.

panels.title: Asked vs used · memory
panels.description: Each bubble is a workload, sized by its pods: its memory request per pod against its working set's maximum over the range. The dashed line is a perfect fit. Hover a bubble for its numbers and the suggested request (p95 × 1.2) and limit (maximum × 1.5), in steps of 16 MiB. States: idle uses under 30 % of its request, fits 30 to 100 %, short more than its request, near limit a container's memory maximum over 80 % of its limit (it wins over the others), unset asks for nothing. A workload is a Deployment, StatefulSet or DaemonSet (kube_pod_owner, and kube_replicaset_owner for a Deployment); per pod, its containers are summed, each at its largest across the pods. Jobs, CronJobs and static pods are left out.

panels.title: Where the memory reservation goes
panels.description: Namespace, then workload. Area is the memory it asks for (request per pod × pods), colour its state, and the label its maximum over the range as a share of that request. States: idle uses under 30 % of its request, fits 30 to 100 %, short more than its request, near limit a container's memory maximum over 80 % of its limit (it wins over the others), unset asks for nothing.

panels.title: At the edge
panels.description: The containers closest to trouble: a memory maximum near its limit (80 %), use over its request (CPU at p95, memory at its maximum), or CPU throttled in over 20 % of its periods. At least four, at most six. Each shows its use over the range (the largest pod), the request dashed, the limit red, and the suggested change: request at p95 × 1.2, memory limit at the maximum × 1.5, rounded up to 10m and 16 MiB.
